text_blocks.snippet: Residents and visitors in Central Illinois are frequently targeted by localized digital, phone, and mail-in fraud. Common schemes include fake government text alerts, online retail or pet scams, and aggressive imposter warnings regarding missed tolls or traffic tickets.

list.snippet: Fake State Agency Texts: Scammers send text messages pretending to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or tollways, claiming you owe overdue fees or face suspended driving privileges.
Online Purchase & Pet Fraud: Fraudsters list items or companion pets online, take payment via unverified peer-to-peer apps, and invent delivery or shipping problems before disappearing.
Imposter & Tech Support Calls: Con artists pose as utility providers, tech support, or law enforcement, using high-pressure threats of immediate arrest or service shutoff.
Charity Solicitations: Fake organizations exploit community empathy after local or seasonal events by calling residents for high-pressure cash or bank routing donations.
Never click links in unsolicited text messages or emails claiming to represent state or federal courts, departments of transportation, or delivery services.
Practice the pause: Verify any urgent financial or legal claim by calling the official agency or organization directly using a trusted, independent phone number.
Reject untrusted payment methods such as wire transfers, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or cash-only courier pickups.
Check active regional reports or log a new incident using the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois.

Report identity theft or fraudulent state communications through the
Illinois Attorney General.
File digital complaints regarding phishing or texts via the Federal Trade Commission.

text_blocks.snippet: If you or someone you know was targeted, let me know how they were contacted (text, phone, or email) and what information was shared so I can give you exact steps to protect your accounts.
